subject: Social Media
title: Propaganda Goes Digital
description: A short lesson to help you apply Propaganda Goes Digital.

hook.text: Nazi propaganda needed printing presses and rallies. Modern propaganda needs only a laptop and a WiFi signal.

buildup.text: Traditional propaganda was expensive and traceable. A government had to own media outlets to control narratives.

discovery.text: Social media democratized propaganda. Anyone can create a fake news site in minutes and reach millions overnight.

twist.text: Digital propaganda is cheaper, faster, and harder to trace. A single operator can run hundreds of fake accounts.

climax.text: The shift matters because scale changed. One person can now do what once required an entire ministry.

punchline.text: Propaganda used to need power. Now it just needs Wi-Fi.

quiz.question: What made digital propaganda more dangerous than traditional propaganda?
options: Cheaper, faster, and harder to trace
